name: Manish Kolachalam

papers.title: Emergent Control via Prior-Based Free Energy Minimization
papers.abstract: Theories of cognition suggest that adaptive behavior may emerge through minimization of surprise associated with sensory states rather than explicit reward maximization. Motivated by this distinction, we present a framework for embodied control based on minimization of deviations from priors over preferred states. The framework explores two complementary regimes of adaptive control: (1) a model-based free-energy planner that performs predictive control through learned world models and trajectory optimization, and (2) a model-free free-energy controller trained through deep policy optimization. Importantly, actions are generated through inference over preferred states and maintenance of predictive continuity rather than optimization of scalar reward signals. Across continuous locomotion, autonomous driving, and underactuated control environments, the framework produces coherent and adaptive behavior without access to explicit environment-defined rewards. In a sparse-reward control setting, the framework learns goal-directed behavior solely from preferred-state priors. Stable locomotion emerges from homeostatic and kinematic priors alone, while model-based free-energy planning yields collision-averse and survival-oriented driving behavior. These results suggest that complex embodied behavior can emerge from minimal, self-supervised, free-energy-based objectives, providing an alternative paradigm to reward-centric reinforcement learning.
